Moon Capital Management an investment management company, recently released its Q3 2026 investor letter. A copy of the letter can be downloaded here. The letter reported that its equity portfolio gained approximately 4% during the first nine months of 2026, compared with an approximately 12% year-to-date return for the S&P 500. The firm noted that market gains remained narrow, with nearly half of S&P 500 constituents declining during the period and the median stock gaining only about 4%. Much of the letter focused on AI investment, as major technology companies are expected to spend approximately $1.2 trillion on capital expenditures in 2027 and another $1.4 trillion in 2028. Although the semiconductor industry has benefited from strong demand, with the S&P Global Semiconductor Index rising approximately 95% through September, Moon Capital questioned whether the enormous infrastructure investments would generate adequate returns. The firm has avoided direct AI investments because it remains uncertain which companies will ultimately capture the economic benefits. The firm remains focused on businesses whose economics it can assess with confidence and whose shares trade at meaningful discounts to estimated intrinsic value. In addition, please check the Fund's top five holdings to know its best picks in 2026.

In its third-quarter 2026 investor letter, Moon Capital Management highlighted stocks like Tencent Music Entertainment Group (NYSE:TME). Tencent Music Entertainment Group (NYSE:TME) operates online music and audio entertainment platforms primarily serving the Chinese market. The one-month return of Tencent Music Entertainment Group (NYSE:TME) was 9.65% while its shares traded between $7.66 and $21.55 over the last 52 weeks. On November 9th, 2026, Tencent Music Entertainment Group (NYSE:TME) stock closed at approximately $9.38 per share, with a market capitalization of about $15.20 billion.

Moon Capital Management stated the following regarding Tencent Music Entertainment Group (NYSE:TME) in its Q3 2026 investor letter:

"We believe the market is valuing TME as a declining music-streaming application when, in reality, it is a high-margin, subscription-driven entertainment platform with a dominant ecosystem, substantial financial assets, and a long runway for growth. The market's pessimism is understandable. Total monthly active users (MAUs) have declined, the company's legacy Social Entertainment business has contracted, and competitor Soda Music has grown rapidly. But we believe investors are focusing on the wrong metrics. A shrinking user base does not necessarily mean a declining business when the users who remain are becoming substantially more valuable. TME is shedding its least profitable users – casual listeners whose unit economics are vastly inferior to paying subscribers."

Since its December 2018 IPO, Tencent Music's paying music subscribers have increased from approximately 34 million to 127 million, while the share of users paying for subscriptions has risen from 6% to 24%. The fund also highlighted the company's improving music-related revenue, stronger content economics, and potential to unlock value through share repurchases. The chart on page 5 of the letter shows the paying-subscriber percentage increasing from 17.1% in 2023 to 24.0% in 2025 (Click Here To Read The Letter In Detail)."

The stock market is showing signs of weakness. The S&P 500 index, which tracks the leading stocks on U.S. markets, is down around 5% from its high. It's not in correction territory, but it could potentially decline further, especially if interest rates continue to rise.

Many investors have been pulling money out of tech stocks and other highly valued investments of late, perhaps as a sign of concern for where the market may be heading. For investors who are worried about a potential market crash, there are three excellent dividend stocks that may be solid options to consider right now: Realty Income (NYSE:O), Chevron (NYSE:CVX), and Pfizer (NYSE:PFE).

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Realty Income

Realty Income is a top real estate investment trust (REIT) that can realistically be a fit for just about any type of portfolio. The dividend income it generates makes the investment a bit of a rarity, as it provides investors with a high yield of around 5.5%, has grown its dividend for decades, and pays monthly.

The REIT's portfolio is highly diverse, which can be extremely valuable for investors looking for safety. Realty Income isn't dependent on the health and strength of just one sector of the economy; instead, it has clients in 96 industries, and yet its occupancy rate is incredibly high at just under 99%.

Realty Income has generated modest returns of 6% for investors over the past year, but the real payoff comes from collecting the dividend it has been growing regularly. Realty Income is the type of stock that all investors can comfortably buy and hold for the long haul.

Chevron

Owning a top oil and gas stock can be vital when market conditions are poor, especially if inflation is high. Chevron's stock soared by more than 50% in 2022 when the market was down big due to inflation. In the past 12 months, it's risen by around 35% due to inflation and rising oil prices, yet again.

Chevron, being the oil and gas giant that it is, benefits from higher commodity prices and can thus be a fairly safe long-term holding, giving investors a valuable way to diversify their portfolios and hedge against adverse market conditions.

Like Realty Income, it has also been raising its payout for decades. If not for its stellar gains this year, its yield would be higher than it is right now. However, even at 3.4%, it's still more than three times the S&P 500 average of 1.1%. This is yet another top dividend stock that investors may want to hang on to for long-term stability.

title: How major US stock indexes fared Tuesday 11/10/2026

How major US stock indexes fared Tuesday 11/10/2026
The Associated Press
Tue, November 10, 2026 at 2:20 PM MST 1 min read
^GSPC
^DJI
^IXIC
^RUT
CL=F

U.S. stocks fell after a report showed inflation was worse across the country last month than economists expected.

The S&P 500 lost 0.4% Tuesday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 0.3%, and the Nasdaq composite fell 0.7%.

The discouraging report on inflation caused traders to up their forecasts for coming hikes to interest rates by the Federal Reserve. One top Fed official even suggested that it could raise its main interest rate by twice the typical amount at its meeting next month. Treasury yields jumped in the bond market even though oil prices continued to ease.

On Tuesday:

The S&P 500 fell 29.01 points, or 0.4%, to 7,520.93.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 157.86 points, or 0.3%, to 52,231.89.

The Nasdaq composite fell 187.26 points, or 0.7%, to 25,065.87.

The Russell 2000 fell 19.44 points, or 0.7%, to 2,821.38.

For the week:

The S&P 500 is up 144.07 points, or 2%.

The Dow is up 946.16 points, or 1.8%.

The Nasdaq is up 486.45 points, or 2%.

The Russell 2000 is up 67.27 points, or 2.4%.

For the year:

The S&P 500 is up 675.43 points, or 9.9%.

The Dow is up 4,168.60 points, or 8.7%.

The Nasdaq is up 1,823.88 points, or 7.8%.

The Russell 2000 is up 339.47 points, or 13.7%.
